question_text: Why do we prefer a spanner of longer arm to a spanner of shorter arm?

steps.margin_note: Same torque idea as the door question — name r as the arm length.
steps.why: A nut turns about its own axis; only torque about that axis loosens it.
common_mistakes: Talking about "more power". The quantity at work is torque, not power.

recall.must_convey: That the turning effect is torque, τ = r F, with r the arm length.

steps.memory_tip: Torque is force times arm. The hand supplies F; the spanner supplies r.

steps.label: The reason
lines: For the same applied force, a longer
arm gives a larger r, so

lines.text: a longer spanner gives more torque.

lines: The nut turns with less effort.
steps.margin_note: Say "for the same force" — that is the comparison the question sets up.
steps.why: Torque trades force for distance. The long arm lets a small hand force do what a large force would need up close.
common_mistakes: Leaving out "same force", which makes the comparison meaningless.

recall.must_convey: That for the same force a longer arm gives more torque, so less effort is needed.

steps.memory_tip: Double the arm and the torque doubles, with the same hand force.

insider_note: Both marks depend on the words "for the same force". Without that phrase no comparison has been made.
